draft.title: Reflections
card: A reflection flips a graph over a line, like a mirror. The flipped graph has the same shape and size.
y = -f(x) reflects the graph in the x-axis. Every y value changes sign, so the point (x, y) moves to (x, -y).
y = f(-x) reflects the graph in the y-axis. Every x value changes sign, so the point (x, y) moves to (-x, y).
Example: the point (2, 5) is on y = f(x). Then (2, -5) is on y = -f(x), and (-2, 5) is on y = f(-x).
draft.remember: A minus outside f flips up and down. A minus inside f flips left and right.

a.q: The point (3, 4) is on y = f(x). Which point must be on y = -f(x)?
a.why: A minus outside f changes the sign of every y value, so (3, 4) moves to (3, -4). The point (-3, 4) is on y = f(-x), because that changes the sign of x instead.
a.clue: The minus is outside f, so it acts on the output.

b.q: The point (-6, 2) is on y = f(x). Which point must be on y = f(-x)?
b.why: A minus inside f changes the sign of every x value, so (-6, 2) moves to (6, 2). The point (-6, -2) is tempting, but it is on y = -f(x), which changes the sign of y.
b.clue: The minus is inside the brackets, so it acts on x.
